quote: Das grosse Problem [-der-] Wissenschaften ist doch immer die {+Thatsachen der+} Anschauung oder die Sinneseindrücke in einen logischen Zusammenhang zu bringen; das geschieht am besten durch die [-A-] axiomatische Methode
english: The great problem of the sciences is always to bring the facts of intuition or the sense impressions into a logical connection; this is best done by the axiomatic method.
topic: Remarks on how the Archimedean axiom and Hilbert's completeness axiom split the usual continuity axiom, followed by reflections on the axiomatic method, mathematics as universal philosophy, and the cheapness of checking mathematical truths.

triage.modern_statement: This is not a mathematical research question. It is a methodological or philosophical statement: the main task of the sciences is to put the facts of intuition and sense impressions into a logical connection, and the axiomatic method is the best way to do that. The closest well-known published counterparts are Hilbert's 6th problem of 1900 (the axiomatization of the physical sciences) and his 1917 Zürich lecture 'Axiomatisches Denken' (Math. Ann. 78, 1918). This diary remark is a programmatic credo rather than a precise question that could be solved.
triage.answered_by: Not applicable. No answer is expected because the note is a statement of method. Hilbert developed the same view publicly in the 6th problem (Paris ICM, 1900) and in 'Axiomatisches Denken' (Zürich lecture 1917, published in Math. Ann. 78, 1918).

evidence.claim: Hilbert's sixth problem (1900) is a programmatic call to axiomatize the physical sciences. It came out of his foundational work in geometry and its link to the empirical sciences; he saw axiomatization as a way to clarify the logical structure of established scientific theories.
Hilbert's 'Axiomatisches Denken' was published in Mathematische Annalen 78 (1917/18), pp. 405–415. It began as a lecture to the Swiss Mathematical Society.
Hilbert believed that developing any scientific subject rigorously required an axiomatic approach.
Work on the axiomatization of physics (the sixth problem) is still being published.

triage.why: The sentence states a philosophy of science (axiomatics as the way to give logical order to empirical facts). It contains no precise mathematical claim that could be proved or refuted. It matches ideas Hilbert published in the 6th problem and in 'Axiomatisches Denken'. The broader program of axiomatizing physics, the 6th problem, is still a research topic, but the note itself is not a problem that could be 'solved'. Its date was not checked.
